answer: Cross-Epoch Pulse Matching. Each identity emits a periodic behavioural pulse—its signed activity timing and interaction graph hash per epoch. Validators retain a rolling record and require a new epoch's pulse to correlate above threshold with the identity's prior spiral of history, allowing gradual drift but not abrupt reinvention. A fresh identity crossing epochs cold must survive several matching rounds before gaining weight; each failed match resets its history and the attacker pays full compute and registration cost again.
